chapter: Europe tours, Birdland memories and closing
title: A snowbound trip back from Boston and carrying his horn
summary: Cobb describes being helped by friend Doc Nepples, the Houston flight being diverted to Kennedy Airport in the snow, and how he packs his horn.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: But you had rather a bad time traveling up there, didn't you?
I had a bad time traveling coming back in that snow, and I didn't have no snow shoes.
And who looked out for you on that --

I had a good friend from Jersey, Doc Nepples. He used to be my tenant in my house over there. He come and pick me up at the airport, took me into New York in the rain, hour late the plane was getting in, but he waited until I got there, then hung out with me, took me to Jersey and then come back and picked me up when I came back from Boston to take me to the airport.
Was he with you when they cancelled and said --
No, he had gone then because he didn't linger on account of the snow. He said, 'I better get on back to Jersey.' He saw that if I got to the airport, and I thought

I was home free, checked my bags through with the skycap, and they gave me my ticket, baggage check ticket, went on down to my gate, checked in, got my boarding ticket, and about three seconds after he gave me my board ticket, said now, on the loudspeaker, "All of you that are headed for Houston on Flight 367 will be transferred to Kennedy Airport." Oh, my God, no. Everybody rose like they was in church, and the preacher said, get up, and started to walking, back up to the steps, and I had -- we had to go to the baggage room and get our baggage to claim them, get them all out where they could ship them over.
Oh, and everybody had to carry their own bag?
No, no, you claim your bag.
Oh.
With your baggage check number.
Yeah.
To send from there to Kennedy. And they sent them by bus. I got everything when I got to Houston. Wasn't none (inaudible).
Just your horn and --
My horn and a valet pack. And I had my shoulder bag with me. I just had three pieces.
Did you check your horn through?
Yeah, I can't handle all that (inaudible) a plane.
No, how could you?

I have to trust them. But this horn I carry, very well compact in the case and it's not like my other horn that it jolts around and may be damaged when I get there, but if you take a look when I get through -- when I get through I show you how it's put in and everything's in grooves.
So it won't move.
Yeah, it won't move. And that's an asset, you know.
